candidates.title: Children's results compared with adult reference ranges, so abnormal values are not highlighted
candidates.description: The viewer is used for all inpatients, but abnormal values are judged against the adult range table only. A child's abnormal result can therefore appear normal on the ward round.

causes.text: Reference ranges come only from the adult range table

candidates.effects: Abnormal paediatric result shown without highlighting
candidates.harm: Delayed treatment of a child, e.g. missed hypoglycaemia or hyperkalaemia

controls.description: Age-banded reference ranges selected from the patient's age
Test cases for paediatric results at range boundaries
Until fixed, hide range highlighting for under-16s and show a banner

candidates.rating_rationale: A missed abnormal result in a child can cause serious harm; children are admitted to this Trust's wards, so it will happen whenever one is reviewed here.
candidates.reasoning: The intended use covers all inpatients, which includes children, and the workflow says highlighting relies on the adult range table. Nothing in the documents describes paediatric ranges.
candidates.assumptions: Assumed children are admitted to wards where this viewer is used, and that there is no separate paediatric results system.

candidates.title: Result acknowledged by one clinician disappears for everyone, so another clinician never sees it
candidates.description: Acknowledging a result removes it from a list shared by everyone on the ward. If it is acknowledged by mistake, or by someone without the full picture, others lose sight of it.

causes.text: Acknowledge removes the result from a shared ward list
Mis-tap on a tablet during a busy round

candidates.effects: Abnormal result no longer visible to the team

controls.description: Show acknowledged results in a separate 'acknowledged today' list with who acknowledged them
Undo for five minutes after Acknowledge
Ward round briefing on what Acknowledge means

candidates.rating_rationale: Shared lists on tablets during busy rounds make accidental acknowledgement plausible; the harm is a delayed response to an abnormal result.
candidates.reasoning: The workflow states that acknowledged results drop off a list shared by everyone on the ward, with no mention of who acknowledged them or of undo.
candidates.assumptions: Assumed acknowledgement is not reversible in the current design.

citations.quote: Acknowledged results drop off the list. The list is shared by everyone logged in on that ward.

causes.text: List refreshes only every five minutes during the round

candidates.effects: Clinician finishes the round without seeing a newly arrived result

controls.description: Push new results to the open list as they arrive, with a 'new since you opened' marker

candidates.rating_rationale: Same harm as H-004; a five-minute gap during a round is a realistic window.
candidates.reasoning: H-004 covers interface backlogs but not the viewer's own refresh interval, which the workflow document states.
